title: "Charter ambiguity — §<section>"
labels: ["charter", "review"]
---

## Charter location

Section number and line range or short quote of the prose under review.

## The ambiguity or drift risk

Describe concretely what reading is available that the author may not have intended, OR what claim fails one of the four falsifiability tests. Be specific about what would falsify the claim and how a third party could detect the violation.

## Falsifiability assessment

If applicable, identify which of the four tests from [`falsifiability-check` §1](../../.claude/skills/epistemic/falsifiability-check/SKILL.md) the claim fails:

- [ ] **1.1 Violation** — no state can be described that makes the claim false.
- [ ] **1.2 Observation** — a violation cannot be detected without subjective judgment or violator cooperation.
- [ ] **1.3 Operationalization** — terms in the claim do not reduce to concrete substrate artifacts.
- [ ] **1.4 Non-circularity** — the claim defines a term using only itself or terms defined using itself.
- [ ] None of the above — the report is about something other than falsifiability.

## Proposed direction

Which resolution kind does the reporter think fits?

- [ ] Editorial fix (typo, formatting, non-meaning change) — see [`amendments.md` §Amendment Discipline](../../docs/charter/amendments.md).
- [ ] Charter amendment (substantive change to FROZEN text) — requires RFC per [`amendments.md` §Amendment Process](../../docs/charter/amendments.md).
- [ ] Open question for committee — surface but do not yet propose a fix.

---

An issue is not an RFC. Substantive changes require a formal RFC per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../CONTRIBUTING.md). Charter ambiguity reports may be promoted to a `charter-amendment` RFC if the maintainers concur.
